Deuterium substitution is a common strategy in adjusting in vivo metabolism, thereby altering the drug’s therapeutic index. Recently, the FDA approved a deuterated TBZ, tetrabenazine-D6 (Austedo, SD-809, Fig. [ref-type: fig] 1 [Source reference: [Source link 25]]), demonstrating extended blood circulation and improved treatment of Huntington’s disease (Frank et al. [ref-type: bibr] 2016 [Source reference: [Source link 26]]). Deuterated DTBZ derivatives, including D6-[^{18}F]FP-(+)-DTBZ and D4-[^{18}F]FE-(+)-DTBZ (Fig. [ref-type: fig] 1 [Source reference: [Source link 27]]), have been reported to enhance the PET signal of VMAT2 by reducing in vivo defluorination (Liu et al. [ref-type: bibr] 2018 [Source reference: [Source link 28]]; Jahan et al. [ref-type: bibr] 2011 [Source reference: [Source link 29]]). Due to this mechanism, the biodistribution of D6-[^{18}F]FP-(+)-DTBZ showed improved striatum/cerebellum uptake ratios in the brains of normal rats (Zhao et al. [ref-type: bibr] 2019 [Source reference: [Source link 30]]). Additionally, a study using D4-[^{18}F]FE-(+)-DTBZ in nonhuman primates demonstrated higher brain uptake with faster washout compared to the nondeuterated [^{18}F]FE-(+)-DTBZ (Liu et al. [ref-type: bibr] 2018 [Source reference: [Source link 31]]; Jahan et al. [ref-type: bibr] 2011 [Source reference: [Source link 32]]).
